 BBC News
 Watch live Summary
 Manchester United sack head coach Michael Carrick - watch live at the top of this page 
 Man Utd release a statement saying the club came to an 'extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary' 
 'Man Utd board deemed results, situation and league position as unacceptable', writes Simon Stone 
 'It is time for the owners to explain themselves' says the Manchester United Supporters' Trust 
 Former Tottenham and Chelsea manager Mauricio Pochettino is 'ready to accept an offer' to replace Carrick - United have 'opened talks' with him
 It follows their 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday, which leaves them sitting in the Premier League's relegation zone
 Carrick took interim charge in January and led club to a third-place finish before signing two-year deal in summer

 'Man Utd have become a laughing stock' published at 12:18 GMT 12:18 GMT 
 Rio Ferdinand 
Former Man Utd defender on YouTube 
 It is tiring, imagine being a player at the club right now. There is just nothing positive to say about Manchester United. 
 The spotlight is on them and they don't want it to be. United have become a laughing stock. 
 The way in which it has been done could have been better and the leaks that have been coming out are terrible and it adds to the disrespect for this situation on him [Carrick] and his family. Even his kids will be feeling this. The minimum he should be getting is respect.

 'The squad is capable of more than it's showing at the moment' published at 12:12 GMT 12:12 GMT 
 Simon Stone 
BBC Sport Manchester United reporter on 5 Live 
 It will be interesting to see whether Manchester United spend the money in January because most people feel that they need more players or different players, certainly in defence maybe up front as well but then Manchester United also have huge debt so how much have they got to spend? 
 Who could they spend it on? 
 It's not entirely clear. I think most fans would say it doesn't really matter who the manager is, whilst the current system is in place, it won't work. 
 I'm pretty sure Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer family have a completely different view of it. 
 The fact that Manchester United finished third last year, albeit they weren't in Europe and they didn't have any cup matches, proves that the squad is capable of more than it's showing at the moment. 
 People at Manchester United not so long ago were saying that squad was capable of a top-five finish, which in the last couple of years would have been enough to finish in the Champions League spots again. 
 At the moment they are 18th and clearly there's a long way between Champions League qualification and 18th.

 'Man Utd will have to pay compensation' published at 11:50 GMT 11:50 GMT 
 Kieran Maguire 
Football finance expert 
 Manchester United will have to pay compensation to Michael Carrick and potentially they would have to also pay compensation to another entity, should that person be in current employment.
 I guess the club will be fully aware that in their current position, should that be maintained, which I think is highly unlikely, that relegation would result in a significant drop in revenue for the club somewhere in the region of £200-250 million. 
 The palate of players that he has to coach, whoever the person is that comes in, will be the same. Certainly if you take a look at the statistical evidence, mid-season changes to managers sometimes work, and it did work, ironically, with Michael Carrick himself. But there are a number of other clubs where it hasn't.

 Man Utd board deemed results this season as 'unacceptable' published at 11:32 GMT 11:32 GMT 
 Simon Stone 
BBC Sport Manchester United reporter 
 Club sources say this week's training schedule was planned a month ago and while they accept Carrick’s treatment this week doesn't look great, given the situation they are not sure what else they could have done.
 United felt justified in handing Carrick a two-year contract in May after he won 12 games out of 17 as interim boss to secure qualification to the Champions League and sources stress the 45-year-old’s "leadership and achievements" since January will always be appreciated and recognised.
 However, there is a brutal reality of a current situation that sees United 18th, and in a relegation place ahead of a trip to Liverpool on 22 November. Internally, as well as externally, this is viewed as "unacceptable". Sources say senior figures at the club share the level of ‘frustration and anger’ of fans at recent performances and at the league position and led to a belief a change had to be made immediately.
 Many felt Carrick should have gone after the 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth on 25 October, which followed straight after the Como horror show, the 4-1 defeat followed by Bruno Fernandes’ post-match outburst. The club wanted to give Carrick a chance to turn the situation round but while there was a stirring 3-2 victory against Roma, a decent first half showing at Chelsea and two two-goal comebacks to snatch a draw against Aston Villa, United’s hierarchy did not see enough to convince them the side were on the right path.
 Whilst there has been huge criticism externally of United’s transfer business in the summer, Old Trafford insiders are adamant the current squad is far better than performances and results so far this season have indicated and believe a different approach will trigger the necessary improvement.
 Outsiders may be sceptical but high level officials are adamant the club is determined to do everything it can to build a club worthy of what is stated as "immense support".

 'It is time for the owners to explain themselves' - MUST published at 11:12 GMT 11:12 GMT 
 Manchester United 
 Manchester United Supporters' Trust have just released a statement. It says: "Michael Carrick’s departure marks another depressing moment for Manchester United. We thank him for his service and for restoring hope during the second half of last season. His standing among supporters remains undiminished.
 "The reason Manchester United fans have continued to support Michael Carrick in recent weeks is that they know that responsibility for United’s problems do not primarily rest with him or indeed his predecessors as manager.
 "They lie with the ownership.
 "The Glazers’ debt-funded takeover continues to burden the club. When INEOS came in they promised sporting excellence, but yet with repeated changes in football leadership we have seen anything but.
 "It is time for the owners to explain themselves and show some accountability."

 'Carrick's staff knew the writing was on the wall' published at 11:00 GMT 11:00 GMT 
 Simon Stone 
BBC Sport Manchester United reporter on 5 Live 
 Football's a strange business at the best of times and clearly, if you are going to dismiss a manager you're going to have another manager in place to take over from him. 
 I think those negotiations have been happening this week. 
 There was also a big meeting of various Ineos executives in Monaco yesterday, that Manchester United's chief executive Omar Berrada was committed to attend to go there. 
 I think that has just led to this process being elongated even though my understanding is that Michael Carrick's staff knew the writing was on the wall on Monday and knew what was going to happen but people are under contract, they have to fulfill their roles until such time as they're told not to.

 How did we get here? published at 10:53 GMT 10:53 GMT 
 Manchester United 
 Manchester United's last match was a thrilling 4-4 with Aston Villa in which the club twice came from two goals down.
 But that left the club in the relegation zone with just eight points from their 10 Premier League matches.
 This week United's chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox met with minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco and discussed Carrick's future at the club.
 Carrick, who had been attending training this week, left United's training base Carrington this morning.
 As Simon Stone reported , the decision to sack Carrick should trigger the arrival of USA men's national team boss Mauricio Pochettino.

 Man Utd confirm Carrick's departure published at 10:41 GMT 10:41 GMT Breaking 
 Manchester United 
 Manchester United have just released a statement, confirming the dismissal of Michael Carrick. 
 It reads: "Michael rejoined the club in January and guided the team to a third-placed Premier League finish by winning 12 out of the remaining 17 games of the 2025-26 season, accumulating the highest points tally in the league during that period.
 "After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.
 "Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club. His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered.
 "The club intends to appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible."
 Image source, Getty Images
